source.title: An accurate flatness measure to estimate the generalization performance of CNN models
source.authors: R. Taleghani; Maryam Mohammadi; Francesco Marchetti

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including results, tables, figures, and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Measures a new CNN-specific relative-flatness score and correlates it with generalization gaps, conceptually testing V7. It also compares optimizer outcomes relevant to V4, using a different setup from the original claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports cited prior findings about batch size, sharpness, and generalization; these are not rows. The report of optimizer trends in Section 5.2.1 has no numerical breakdown by optimizer, so it is recorded as a qualitative result. Figure-only label-noise and transfer-learning findings are not assigned values.
record.test_reason: The study tests the magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization relationship in V7 using weight-magnitude-weighted Hessian curvature, an alternative to finite perturbation tolerance. Its optimizer comparison reports generalization gaps without establishing worse held-out performance, so it does not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' central conclusion: their exact final-layer relative-curvature measure is proposed as a practical generalization diagnostic, with causality left unresolved. Their stronger claim of consistent tracking across architectures and augmentation settings needs qualification: VGG-16 correlations are very weak, and augmentation-group means do not follow the within-group relationship.
record.recipe_differences: The paper measures a convolutional relative-flatness score based on a derived Hessian trace, rather than scaled weight perturbation tolerance; it reports correlations with generalization gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported correlation strength differs by architecture (VGG-16 versus DenseNet-121 and ResNet-18) and by training condition; optimizer and learning-rate choices are described as affecting flatness and gaps. Augmentation protocols also shift the reported flatness and generalization gap.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD with momentum has smaller reported generalization gaps than AdamW across the tested learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects the training-to-validation loss gap; this alone does not establish which optimizer achieves better held-out performance.

fits_no_version.finding: During transfer learning, final symbolic curvature correlates negatively with test accuracy (Spearman ρ = −0.68).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final-layer relative curvature tracks transfer accuracy across fine-tuning strategies; training-to-test gaps are not reported for this comparison.

record.code_released: The authors state the code is in a GitHub private repository; no URL is stated.
record.problems: The authors note that the observed correlations do not establish causality. Results are limited to CNNs with a GAP head and a relative-flatness measure of the final convolutional layer. The optimizer comparison is qualitative in the text, and some findings are shown only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only label-noise trends and transfer-learning trends are not included because the supplied text does not give assignable values for the relevant figure results. Section 5.6 stopping-strategy results are not extracted because they compare stopping rules and do not directly test a listed version.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy. Partial label corruption does not establish this comparison.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Optimizer-specific held-out performance under limited versus broader tuning, matched training performance, switching optimizers, and language-model results.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, excessive dropout, and removal of dropout with weight decay.

Finite magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance before training error rises; ranking against norm- and margin-based measures; SVHN; and systematic verification that compared networks reach similarly low training loss.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence and comparing retrained accuracy with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Lower κ denotes flatter solutions; positive κ–gap correlations therefore have the predicted direction. Evidence concerns an alternative magnitude-aware curvature measure, not direct replication of Jiang et al.'s perturbation-tolerance measure. No original-source exclusion applies. Figure-only label-noise and transfer findings were declared omitted, so they are not missing rows.

versions.untested_parts: Image and language benchmark breadth; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptation of the training recipe.
Dropout comparisons and its interaction with weight decay and augmentation.
Weight-perturbation tolerance scaled to weight magnitudes; comparison against norm- and margin-based measures; the cited sharpness counterexamples.
Removing memorized examples and comparing test accuracy after retraining.

rows.subject: 84 independent models on Modified ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Measured the association between convolutional relative flatness κ(K) and generalization gap across the 84 models.

conditions.value: learning rates, batch sizes, and multiple random seeds varied

rows.measure: Flatness versus generalization-gap correlation; Spearman ρ = 0.7621, p = 3.775 × 10−17; Pearson r = 0.5803, 95% CI [0.4179, 0.7067], p = 7.244 × 10−9; R² = 0.3367.
rows.value: Higher flatness was associated with larger generalization gaps; the reported correlations are above.
rows.uncertainty: 95% CI [0.4179, 0.7067] for Pearson r; p-values as stated.
rows.note: Aggregate relationship across 84 models; the study reports correlation, not causal evidence or magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance.
rows.check: The positive association has the predicted direction: higher κ means sharper, rather than flatter, solutions. The backbone was pretrained on ImageNet before CIFAR-10 training. Comparable low training losses across all 84 models are not established.

rows.subject: Modified ResNet-18 models, SGD with Momentum (sgd mom)
rows.operation_detail: Compared optimizer-associated flatness and generalization-gap trends across tested learning rates.
rows.measure: Generalization gap and final flatness, described comparatively without numerical optimizer-specific values.
rows.baseline: AdamW trends in the same comparison
rows.value: Consistently lower generalization gap and flatter minima than AdamW across tested learning rates.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison; optimizer-specific numbers are not given in the text.
rows.check: A smaller validation-minus-training loss gap does not establish better held-out performance without the underlying training and validation losses. The qualitative optimizer comparison cannot determine V4.

rows.subject: Modified ResNet-18 models, AdamW
rows.operation_detail: Compared optimizer-associated flatness and generalization-gap trends across tested learning rates.
rows.measure: Generalization gap and final flatness, described comparatively without numerical optimizer-specific values.
rows.baseline: SGD with Momentum trends in the same comparison
rows.value: AdamW tended to reach sharper minima and a larger, more unstable generalization gap; flatness was often much higher, especially at learning rates 0.005 and 0.01.
rows.note: Qualitative result; the paper describes spread and outliers but gives no optimizer-specific gap values.
rows.check: A larger generalization gap does not establish worse held-out performance. Neither optimizer-specific held-out losses nor matched training performance are reported.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Reported correlation between flatness and generalization gap across runs.
rows.note: Weak association compared with other architectures in this table.
rows.check: The association is very weak: Pearson r = 0.076 and Spearman ρ = 0.118. These values do not justify the authors' description of a consistently useful relationship across architectures; significance is not reported.

rows.subject: DenseNet-121
rows.operation_detail: Reported correlation between flatness and generalization gap across runs.
rows.note: Correlation is positive but weaker than the reported ResNet-18 aggregate Spearman correlation.
rows.check: The positive relationship is appreciably weaker than the main ResNet-18 result, especially for rank correlation: ρ = 0.443 versus 0.7621.

rows.subject: Modified ResNet-18 models
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10; 20 independent runs per condition
rows.operation_detail: Measured flatness and generalization gap separately under no augmentation.
rows.measure: Test accuracy 73.5 ± 0.4%; generalization gap 0.265 ± 0.004; flatness κl 2.51 ± 0.42; correlation ρ = 0.584.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation across 20 runs; correlation uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The correlation is positive; this is a condition-specific measurement.
rows.check: Table 6 reports a positive within-condition correlation. However, Appendix C.2.2 describes near-zero baseline variance and undefined regression statistics, requiring caution. Its reported gap also equals one minus test accuracy, whereas Section 5.2 defines a cross-entropy loss gap.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.5, Table 6, p. 24; Appendix C.2.2, p. 35
source_check.problem: The reported values match; Appendix C.2.2 nevertheless describes near-zero baseline variance and undefined regression R² and p-values.

rows.subject: Modified ResNet-18 models
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10; 20 independent runs per condition
rows.operation_detail: Measured flatness and generalization gap separately under basic augmentation.
rows.measure: Test accuracy 82.1 ± 0.4%; generalization gap 0.179 ± 0.004; flatness κl 4.33 ± 0.49; correlation ρ = 0.691.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation across 20 runs; correlation uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The correlation is positive; this is a condition-specific measurement.
rows.check: The within-condition correlation supports the predicted direction. Across augmentation conditions, however, this condition has higher κ and a smaller gap than no augmentation. The reported gap equals one minus test accuracy rather than an explicitly documented loss difference.

rows.operation_detail: Measured flatness and generalization gap separately under AutoAugment.
rows.measure: Test accuracy 82.2 ± 0.6%; generalization gap 0.178 ± 0.006; flatness κl 4.69 ± 0.40; correlation ρ = 0.702.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation across 20 runs; correlation uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The correlation is positive; this is a condition-specific measurement.
rows.check: The within-condition correlation supports the predicted direction. Across augmentation conditions, however, this condition has higher κ and a smaller gap than no augmentation. The reported gap equals one minus test accuracy rather than an explicitly documented loss difference.

rows.subject: Modified ResNet-18 models
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10; 20 independent runs per condition
rows.operation_detail: Measured flatness and generalization gap separately under Mixup.
rows.measure: Test accuracy 80.6 ± 1.1%; generalization gap 0.194 ± 0.011; flatness κl 5.04 ± 0.41; correlation ρ = 0.725.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation across 20 runs; correlation uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The correlation remains positive under Mixup.
rows.check: The within-condition correlation supports the predicted direction. Compared with no augmentation, the mean κ increases while the gap decreases. The reported gap equals one minus test accuracy rather than an explicitly documented loss difference.

relationships.condition: Modified ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, 84 models; alternative relative-curvature measure
relationships.reason: R1 reports larger gaps for higher magnitude-aware curvature, with Spearman ρ = 0.7621 and Pearson r = 0.5803; this supports the association through an alternative sharpness measure.
relationships.display_finding: Higher curvature accompanied larger reported gaps (Spearman ρ = 0.7621; Pearson r = 0.5803), although the paper's gap definitions were inconsistent.

source_check.reason: R1 reports positive curvature–gap correlations, ρ=0.7621 and r=0.5803; lower κ denotes flatter solutions. Support concerns the alternative-measure association.

relationships.reason: R4 reports only a very weak relationship, with Spearman ρ = 0.118 and Pearson r = 0.076.
relationships.display_finding: Curvature correlated only very weakly with the reported generalization gap (Spearman ρ = 0.118; Pearson r = 0.076). The gap definitions were inconsistent.

relationships.display_finding: Curvature had a moderate correlation with the reported generalization gap (Spearman ρ = 0.443), weaker than the corresponding correlation for ResNet-18. The gap definitions were inconsistent.

relationships.condition: Within each ResNet-18 augmentation protocol on CIFAR-10
relationships.reason: R6–R9 report positive within-condition rank correlations of 0.584–0.725; the no-augmentation estimate has a conflicting low-variance description in Appendix C.2.2.
relationships.display_finding: Within each protocol, rank correlations between curvature and the reported generalization gap were positive (0.584–0.725). The unaugmented baseline had conflicting descriptions of its variance, and the gap definitions were inconsistent.

relationships.display_finding: Unaugmented models had lower mean curvature yet larger reported gaps than augmented models, although the paper's gap definitions were inconsistent.
